summary: Runtime binding requires the complete primary-plus-remaster resource graph and native publication/lifetime ownership. Current offline manifests and disk hashes do not bind subsequent loader reads. A bounded owned-handoff design is identified, but no runtime handoff or safe rollback is implemented or claimed.

claims.Finding: Creates the CFileMan named semaphore with requested initial count and maximum count 1; stores the handle at object+24.
claims.Limitations: This is a semaphore, not an owner-tracking recursive mutex; CreateSemaphore failure is not handled here.

claims.Finding: Waits indefinitely on object+24 and returns WaitForSingleObject status.
claims.Limitations: The calling 3F9850 body does not check this status. Acquiring it and then calling that loader would attempt another wait.

claims.Finding: Releases one semaphore count; a failed ReleaseSemaphore returns GetLastError.
claims.Limitations: It provides no ownership token and does not demonstrate that arbitrary other callers are serialized.

claims.Finding: Allocates a 344-byte CFileMan, initializes its thread handle to zero, creates the count-1 semaphore and selects package mode 3.
claims.Limitations: The historical IDB comment says it starts a thread; the complete body does not. Worker creation is separately established at16C9D0. It also lacks allocation/handle failure recovery.

claims.Finding: CFileMan deletion closes its semaphore via FDAA0, then runs CThread cleanup FD950 before optionally freeing the object.
claims.Limitations: Neither callee joins the resource worker. This claim concerns these exact destructors, not every shutdown path.

claims.Finding: CThread cleanup closes nonnull handles at +24 and +8 and clears the fields; it does not call WaitForSingleObject.
claims.Limitations: Closing a handle is not a join or proof that another thread has stopped.

claims.Finding: Package teardown frees each current metadata table and HED buffer, closes its PKG descriptor, frees the PackageFile, nulls the array entry, then resets selected index and count.
claims.Limitations: The inspected body does not acquire CFileMan's semaphore. An app pointer alone is not a package lifetime guarantee.

claims.Finding: After the application-loop call105420 returns, startup's enclosing function tears down package providers via1064D0 before AppInterface destruction.
claims.Limitations: Existing live app/global pointer values cannot by themselves attest that providers are still alive during shutdown. Startup package order was documented previously.

claims.Finding: File lookup mutates the global selected package index79CFD4 while iterating registered packages79CFE0, and invokes their FindAndPrepare callback.
claims.Limitations: It can wait for package registration and mutate prepared state; it is not a read-only existence probe.

claims.Finding: FindAndPrepare reuses an equal cached name without re-reading PKG metadata; otherwise it mutates name+344, record offset+24, header+300, seed+328 and remaster table+320.
claims.Limitations: The cached string has no source-content identity or generation. Existing HED/record bounds and transform semantics remain separately documented.

claims.Finding: Package metadata cleanup frees +320 and clears the cached name when that table was nonnull.
claims.Limitations: Prepared metadata pointers cannot be retained across preparation/cleanup; there is no generation field in this body.

claims.Finding: The normal package reader selects a provider, reads primary bytes, checks returned length against package+300, then optionally invokes12F070(name,length,destination).
claims.Limitations: Successful registration is not a content-validity or all-allocation-success proof. The decompiler omits forwarded arguments at the12F070 call; ASM retains them.

claims.Finding: The worker-facing loader retires overlapping ResourceEntry state before acquiring the file semaphore, calls106700(register=1) under it, releases it, then attaches the current ResourceEntry pointer to a BAR header.
claims.Limitations: Only this inner load/registration interval is established under the semaphore. Cleanup before it and BAR header writes afterward are outside that interval; mode!=3 has another registration path.

claims.Finding: ASM preserves incoming name RCX, logical length EDX and primary pointer R8; it strips the configured prefix and forwards all three to12E5C0.
claims.Limitations: The legacy inferred one-argument prototype is incomplete. No new C-callable hook ABI is implemented here.

claims.Finding: Creates a1672-byte ResourceEntry, updates replacement-context current entry, inserts it into the resource list and may dispatch a registered handler; a negative constructor status removes the entry.
claims.Limitations: This mutates global state and calls arbitrary registered handlers. It is not safe staging or a pure parser; allocation failures are not fully handled.

claims.Finding: Computes a primary-buffer MD5 before later BAR mutations, then in package mode3 repeatedly fetches current remaster count, allocated payload, name and ID; retained payloads become120-byte ReplaceEntry objects with data+96 and size+80.
claims.Limitations: Primary digest does not bind remaster bytes. Region/name filtering may discard a payload immediately. The constructor can return failure after earlier replacement allocations and exposes native string/index assumptions.

claims.Finding: Returns count+304 from the globally selected PackageFile, rather than from a resource-local immutable descriptor.
claims.Limitations: Call requires a valid current selected index/provider; it carries no resource identity argument.

claims.Finding: Replaces RCX with globally selected PackageFile and tailcalls107760, preserving output-size RDX and index R8D.
claims.Limitations: This explains the actual three-argument remaster ABI; a future binding must check the passed and selected provider agree.

claims.Finding: Returns a borrowed48-byte metadata row from selected PackageFile+320 and writes row+36 ID through RDX.
claims.Limitations: The signed upper-bound check does not reject negative indices. Borrowed row lifetime ends on table replacement/free.

claims.Finding: Allocates an aligned remaster buffer, seeks the prepared offset in the selected PKG descriptor and applies row size/mode plus package seed to read/decode.
claims.Limitations: It does not prove exact read or inflate success. Its returned allocation is later owned by ReplaceEntry; allocation compatibility is part of any replacement implementation.

claims.Finding: Package mode3 bypasses replacement name_table file loading; other modes can acquire the same file semaphore while loading name tables and selecting region aliases.
claims.Limitations: A proposed in-lock handoff must restrict and revalidate mode3; it cannot assume all modes are nonrecursive.

claims.Finding: ReplaceEntry destruction calls the retail _aligned_free on its nonnull data pointer at+96, clears that pointer, and optionally frees the entry.
claims.Limitations: A borrowed ticket buffer or memory allocated by an incompatible allocator must not be passed as a native-owned replacement.

claims.Finding: ResourceEntry destruction removes and destroys its ReplaceEntry list, then calls12D5A0 on its primary metadata and optionally frees itself.
claims.Limitations: It does not free the primary pointer itself in this body. Primary storage ownership belongs to the resource graph and cannot be inferred from replacement ownership.

claims.Finding: Conditional resource destruction can create directories and write1024 bytes of name_table data when the metadata count/state gate is positive.
claims.Limitations: This is another reason not to construct and destroy native registrations as supposedly read-only validation probes.

claims.Finding: Entry removal invokes the registered release callback when present, detaches replacement associations when requested, unlinks the entry, and calls its deleting destructor.
claims.Limitations: A release is not a side-effect-free rollback; registered callbacks and native resource owners may already observe it.

claims.Finding: Initialization registers3A0C60 in the worker-slot system and3A0790 as outer-scheduler priority400000 completion task.
claims.Limitations: This separates resource loading from game-thread completion; CFileMan itself is not this worker.

claims.Finding: Selects one of two48-byte worker slots, stores callback/argument, allocates a count0,max1 wake semaphore, and starts its native thread wrapper.
claims.Limitations: No epoch is created for resource requests or provider/cache contents.

claims.Finding: Stores callback/context and calls CreateThread with16C9B0, then sets the requested priority.
claims.Limitations: The supplied old stack-address parameter is not used as thread ownership; a native OS worker is explicitly created.

claims.Finding: The Windows thread entry calls its stored function pointer with the adjacent argument and returns0 if that callback returns.
claims.Limitations: The selected worker wrapper and3A0C60 normally loop; this leaf does not provide cancellation.

claims.Finding: Loops over its selected slot callback and waits on that slot's semaphore when the callback returns.
claims.Limitations: This body has no stop condition or generation publication; it is not a safe quiescence API.

claims.Finding: The worker picks a pending request, sets phase1, runs the loader, prepares BAR replacements before setting phase2, and waits when no pending request exists.
claims.Limitations: A validation observer after phase2 is too late for worker-side parsing. This confirms the prior preconstructor finding with fresh ASM.

claims.Finding: The outer-scheduler completion task sees phase2, runs3A6840 fixup for a nonempty payload, invokes the completion callback and retires the request node.
claims.Limitations: A request-node address can be recycled. Node phase or resource pointer alone is not a durable binding token.

claims.Finding: When idle, the resource worker waits through FDD90 on each nonnull worker wake semaphore.
claims.Limitations: A momentary waiting count is not a durable lease and does not prevent another wake.

claims.Finding: The timing path waits on its separate semaphore and then signals worker wake semaphores through FDC70.
claims.Limitations: Game timing can wake resource work; a post-update host snapshot does not serialize later loader execution.

claims.Finding: Increments a waiter counter, waits indefinitely on semaphore+8, then decrements the counter.
claims.Limitations: The counter tracks waiters, not ownership, successful publication, resource generation or termination.

claims.Finding: Signals a wake semaphore only when its waiter counter is nonzero.
claims.Limitations: This is wake coordination, not a resource-manager lock or join.

claims.Finding: Initializes a global unordered-map sentinel/list, initial bucket mask7/count8 and load factor1, then registers destruction45330.
claims.Limitations: The map tracks metadata, not file handles or content digests; runtime initialization success is not observed.

claims.Finding: With cache enabled, an existing key made from PackageFile+344 causes immediate return. Otherwise it copies prepared rows, may discover remaster files, and inserts or replaces the cache value.
claims.Limitations: Cache hit does not refresh filesystem state; no source timestamp, hash or generation is checked in this body.

claims.Finding: Registered raw loads insert raw-file remaster rows into the filename cache, close the primary raw file and only then call retail12F070. Registered loose loads close the loose file, runFA50, then register.
claims.Limitations: The primary read and subsequent remaster reads use separate opens. This new binding gap is independent of the previously proven five-priority primary reader.

claims.Finding: The FindAndPrepare hook temporarily restores original target bytes, calls the original, reinstalls its patch and on success restores the full request name into PackageFile+344.
claims.Limitations: Hook installation must account for this self-modifying chain. A one-time prologue hash or naive stacked detour does not attest a stable call target.

claims.Finding: Replacement-count hook looks up the globally selected package's filename; cache hit returns vector byte length/48, otherwise native package+304.
claims.Limitations: It builds a temporary string and is not a harmless raw-field getter suitable for an unsafe probe.

claims.Finding: Replacement-name hook returns cached row pointer/ID when a key and index match, otherwise temporarily disables its detour and calls the original.
claims.Limitations: The pointer is borrowed from a mutable vector; same filename or same map node does not preserve its lifetime.

claims.Finding: Replacement-data hook selects cached or package rows, then independently reopens raw source or searches loose remastered sources. Raw uses cached offset/size/mode with a newly read16-byte raw header; absent loose replacement falls back to original remaster reading.
claims.Limitations: This can combine primary bytes/metadata from one read with later replacement bytes from another. File semaphore serialization does not freeze disk contents or higher-priority file appearance.

claims.Finding: Map insertion allocates72-byte nodes containing string at+16 and vector begin/end/capacity at+48/+56/+64. Existing key assignment delegates to13780.
claims.Limitations: An existing node identity does not establish stable row contents or storage; map updates do not publish a content generation.

claims.Finding: Metadata-vector assignment overwrites existing elements or frees/reallocates its buffer when capacity is insufficient; it updates end/capacity pointers.
claims.Limitations: Any borrowed cache row can become stale after an update, including updates of the same filename.

claims.Finding: Lookup masks the supplied FNV hash into a bucket and compares key length and exact bytes to select a node.
claims.Limitations: Equality is filename identity, not primary/remaster byte identity.

claims.Finding: Vector destruction frees its backing allocation using its allocator alignment convention and zeroes begin/end/capacity.
claims.Limitations: External code cannot retain cached-row pointers through destruction or assignment.

claims.Finding: Map-list destruction walks nodes, destroys each metadata vector and string, frees nodes and finally the sentinel.
claims.Limitations: The examined map teardown provides no reader join, cache generation or shared reader lease.

claims.Finding: The registered exit callback destroys buckets and then the cache list.
claims.Limitations: This is a destruction boundary, not a reload notification or safe host query point.

knownRemainingGaps: No published provider/cache generation binds host staging to the actual consuming worker.
Cache filename equality does not bind metadata vectors to content; raw and loose remaster sources are reopened after primary read.
Resource registration mutates state and can parse/dispatch before a late Drive constructor checkpoint.
The whole target graph, both hands, recursive dependencies, region-selected animation/motion and existing resource reuse need binding before NativeBegin.
The supported hook chain rewrites its own targets when calling originals; coherent observer/handoff installation and exception behavior remain unimplemented.
Native allocation/constructor failure and post-Begin rejection still lack a complete rollback contract.
correctionsToInheritedAnnotations: 107180 initializes a CFileMan semaphore, not the actual resource thread. Fresh16C9D0 proves the separate worker CreateThread.
12F070's inferred one-argument pseudocode is incomplete: the full ASM preserves RCX/EDX/R8 name/length/payload.
deduplication: 56 complete captures include supporting and previously documented functions. They are not56 newly understood functions. Claims are module-labelled and must be deduplicated against earlier research; no full-semantic-review status is asserted.
limitations: Static exact-build proof only; no live provider/cache/hook state sampled.
No native loader probes, interception, process access, file/mod/save writes, product/test edits, package rebuild or coverage update performed.
A proposed binding design is a future implementation contract with explicit unresolved conditions, not a shipped safety guarantee.
